question.explanation:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

\[ V = \dfrac43 \pi r^3, \]

question.text: What is the volume of a sphere whose diameter is $8 \: \textrm{mm}?$
question.explanation:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

\[ V = \dfrac 4 3 \pi r^3, \]

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $r=\dfrac{8}{2} = 4 \: \textrm{mm}$ into the formula, we obtain

\[ V = \dfrac 4 3 \pi \cdot 4^3 = \dfrac{256}{3}\pi \:\textrm{mm}^3. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Radius or Diameter of a Sphere Given Its Volume

question.text: What is the radius of a sphere whose volume is $320\pi \textrm{ cm}^3?$
question.explanation:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

\[ V = \dfrac 4 3 \pi r^3, \]

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $V=320\pi \: \textrm{in}^3$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} V &= \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \\[5pt] 320\pi &= \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \\[5pt] 320\pi \cdot \dfrac{3}{4\pi} &= r^3 \\[5pt] r^3 &= 240. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\[ r =\sqrt[3]{240}= 2\sqrt[3]{30} \: \textrm{cm}. \]

example.title: Finding the Radius or Diameter of a Sphere Given Its Volume

question.text: What is the radius of a sphere whose volume is $\dfrac{343}{6}\pi\:\textrm{ft}^3?$
question.explanation:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula \[ V=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3, \] where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $V=\dfrac{343}{6}\pi\:\textrm{ft}^3$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} V &= \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \\[5pt] \dfrac{343}{6}\pi &= \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \\[5pt] \dfrac{343\pi \cdot 3}{6\cdot4\pi} &= r^3 \\[5pt] r^3 &= \dfrac{343}{8} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7^3}{2^3} \\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^3. \end{align*}

Therefore, \[ r = \sqrt[3]{\left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^3} = \dfrac{7}{2}\:\textrm{ft}. \]
